extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the NEH Public Scholars program (independent writers, researchers, journalists, and other individual book authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for preparing and submitting an NEH Public Scholars grant application to support a nonfiction book for general readers, including eligibility, required materials, research/documentation expectations, period-of-performance rules, and review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal audience: general readers primary
rubrics_metrics.description: The program supports books conceived and written for a general audience; professional scholars should not be the primary audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although proposed books may make a scholarly contribution and be of interest to professional scholars, such readers should not be the primary audience. If your book is primarily addressed to scholars, apply to NEH Fellowships, Summer Stipends, or Awards for Faculty (if affiliated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility: independent scholars allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent writers, researchers, scholars, and journalists may apply; lack of an academic affiliation does not place you at a disadvantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applicants must propose a significant book for general audiences and present evidence of qualifications, including previous publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous publications requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have not published a book with a trade or university press, you must have published at least three articles or essays in general-interest publications that reach a large national or international audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section C1 of the NOFO for details. A nonfiction book with a trade/university press also satisfies the requirement (the book need not have been intended for general readers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'general-interest publication'
rubrics_metrics.description: General-interest publications appeal to a wide variety of readers, present a mix of topics, have a large national/international readership, an editorial staff, and a selective submissions process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: many newspapers and magazines sold at airport newsstands. Excludes peer-reviewed academic journals, edited scholarly volumes, and websites aimed primarily at disseminating scholarly research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical eligibility: humanistic methods required for social-science topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects in social-science areas may be eligible provided their methods are humanistic and do not rely primarily on statistical or mathematical analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Areas that may be eligible include anthropology, sociology, archaeology, linguistics, political science, economics, international relations, psychology, and geography — if approached with humanistic methods. Contact publicscholar@neh.gov if uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student status exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Students enrolled in a degree program at the application deadline or during the proposed grant period are not eligible to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations are ineligible (individual projects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Translation projects by an individual scholar are not eligible for Public Scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If affiliated, consider Fellowships or Summer Stipends; teams of two or more collaborators working on a translation should apply to Scholarly Editions and Translations program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative projects: awards not divisible
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not divide an award among collaborators; co-authors must each submit separate applications specifying individual contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External reviewers will evaluate each application on its own merits. See C3 of the NOFO for additional collaborative-project information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissertation revision ineligible for Public Scholars
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not apply to the Public Scholars program to revise and publish your dissertation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider NEH Fellowships, Summer Stipends, or Awards for Faculty instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language guidance for non-English books
rubrics_metrics.description: Books or writing samples in languages other than English are not prohibited but are discouraged because reviewers may lack language competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All application materials apart from the writing sample must be in English. Address how the language of the proposed book will affect its reach among general readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applications and accepting awards
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply to other NEH programs for the same project, but you generally may accept only one NEH individual award with overlapping periods of performance or supporting the same tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If offered more than one award, you usually may accept only one; accepting a Public Scholars award will automatically withdraw pending Fellowship applications for the same project (exceptions apply). See C3 of the NOFO for details and contact program staff with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent deadlines and award acceptance restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply to Public Scholars and to other NEH programs with adjacent deadlines, but you may not accept awards in both programs if they are for the same project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: applying to Public Scholars in August and Summer Stipends in September is allowed, but you may not accept awards in both programs if both support the same work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application help: staff assistance limited
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH staff will answer questions about preparing your proposal and eligibility but will not comment on draft proposals for this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact publicscholar@neh.gov for questions; staff cannot provide feedback on drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project title guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Title should be descriptive, substantive, free of specialized language, and understandable to the general public; maximum 125 characters (including spaces and punctuation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the title in section 6.a. of the SF-424 Individual Form; NEH reserves the right to retitle funded projects for clarity, although you may use your preferred title for award products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Links to supplementary material
rubrics_metrics.description: You may include links to supplementary material and to publications on your resume, but NEH cannot guarantee links will function or that reviewers will take linked material into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: No changes to application after deadline (with narrow exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not change your application or add material after the application deadline, except for the two letters of reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are submitting a letter of interest or a publisher commitment, you must include it before the deadline. A contract offered after the deadline may not be added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review of eligible applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All eligible applications receive peer review according to NEH procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details about the review process are available (link referenced in FAQ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to reviewers' comments
rubrics_metrics.description: You may request reviewers' comments after notification of the decision on your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsuccessful, reviewers' comments may help revise the application for resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable research methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic research methods (interviews, internet research) are acceptable but may not be sufficient on their own to present a full picture for general readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider additional methods such as consulting previous publications, archival research, or contacting humanities scholars. In the 'Significance and appeal' section, discuss how your project relates to previous work and what new contribution you will make.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable sources
rubrics_metrics.description: A wide variety of primary and secondary sources are acceptable, including documents, books, artifacts, creative works, print/digital publications, digital resources, interviews, observation, surveys, and other fieldwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Sources and organization' section should explain your sources, how you will use them, and how they support your treatment of the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation thoroughness
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation must be thorough enough to demonstrate how you know what you are telling your reader; avoid fabrication and plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: in a biography, be careful to mark speculation and avoid introducing unsupported detail. NEH has a research misconduct policy addressing fabrication and plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of documentation and readability balance
rubrics_metrics.description: The form of documentation (footnotes, endnotes, etc.) is up to you and your publisher, but you should balance readability, thoroughness, and precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent footnotes may annoy general readers; endnotes keyed to phrases may be preferable if they do not introduce ambiguity. The writing sample should demonstrate how you will handle documentation or explain it in the 'Final product and dissemination' section if the sample is from other work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapting scholarly work for general readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars must demonstrate appeal and intellectual significance for general readers; superficial conversion of academic writing is usually insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Go beyond fewer notes or glossary terms: provide a stronger motivation for why the topic matters to general readers, use storytelling, shorten chapters, limit examples, and return regularly to the big picture. Relegate scholarly debates and names to notes and bibliography when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum period of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum period of performance is six full-time months (or the equivalent amount of part-time or combined work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH will reject applications requesting a period of performance shorter than six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting work toward minimum requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not count work done before or after the period of performance toward the six-month minimum requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity and minimum effort during period
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of performance must be continuous and you must work at least half-time on your project throughout it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working part- and full-time in different months can still constitute a continuous period of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part-time/full-time combination and award amount calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards may be held part-time or in combination of part- and full-time work. Award amount reflects equivalent full-time months (e.g., $5,000 per full-time month).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: working half-time for six months equals three full-time months; award would be $30,000 (6 full-time months at $5,000/month) [note: example appears in guidance].

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum period of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Period of performance may not exceed 12 months, even if it includes part-time work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications for letters of reference
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will notify applicants by email when each letter of reference has been received; you can also check letter status in NEH secure area after Grants.gov notifies receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See D7 of the NOFO for other submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and troubleshooting letters of reference
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will not send requests for letters until 3–4 weeks after the application deadline; missing email requests are usually due to junk filters or incorrect addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may resend the link to letter writers by logging into NEH's secure area; contact program staff to correct email address errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing letter writer after deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: You may change a letter writer after the application deadline by contacting program staff with the replacement's contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late letters of reference accepted (possible reviewer exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will automatically add letters uploaded after the deadline to your file, but external reviewers who have already reviewed your application may not take late letters into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing letters do not disqualify
rubrics_metrics.description: A missing letter of reference does not disqualify the application, but reviewers may find the application less persuasive if letters are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional vs. unaffiliated letter writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters from someone at your own institution are allowed, but reviewers may regard letters more highly if at least one is from someone unaffiliated with your institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation of submission responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the applicant's responsibility to confirm that Grants.gov and NEH have received the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Grants.gov's 'Track my Application' tool and see D4 of the NOFO for submission dates and times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov applicant profile requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply, you must set up an 'individual applicant' profile in Grants.gov; the 'Apply' button will not work without it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section 3 of the NOFO for Grants.gov registration instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: UEI requirement for affiliated individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals affiliated with a U.S. institution must provide the institution's UEI number so the institution's name is listed correctly in NEH databases and on the cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies even though the program is for individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing temporary/adjunct affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: If you hold an adjunct or other temporary position at an academic institution at the application deadline, you may list that affiliation on the application form if you wish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing an affiliation will not preclude consideration as an independent scholar; reviewers will consult your resume to understand employment status more fully.
